title: Shared Responsibility Model
definition: A cloud security framework dictating that the Cloud Provider is responsible for the security *OF* the cloud (hardware, physical buildings), and the Customer is responsible for security *IN* the cloud (passwords, firewalls, app code).
simpleExplanation: If someone physically breaks into the Amazon data center with a crowbar, it is Amazon's fault. If someone hacks into your database because your password was '12345', it is your fault.
realWorldExample: A company uses AWS EC2. AWS guarantees the physical server won't be stolen. But the company fails to update their Linux OS, gets hacked via a malware virus, and sues AWS. The judge dismisses it, citing the Shared Responsibility Model: updating Linux was the customer's job.

basic: Who is responsible for locking the front door of the actual data center?
intermediate: In a PaaS (Platform as a Service) model, does the customer have MORE or LESS security responsibility than in an IaaS model?

answers.question: More or less in PaaS?
answers.answer: Less. In PaaS, the provider takes over responsibility for updating the Operating System and Network firewalls. The customer is only responsible for their App Code and Data.

diagramContent:
graph TD
  subgraph Customer Responsibility (Security IN the Cloud)
    Data[Customer Data]
    IAM[Identity & Access Management]
    OS[Operating System / Firewall Rules]
  end

  subgraph AWS/GCP Responsibility (Security OF the Cloud)
    Compute[Compute & Storage Hardware]
    Network[Global Infrastructure]
    Physical[Datacenter Security Guards]
  end

  Data --> IAM
  IAM --> OS
  OS -.-> Compute
